samples.summary: relativeRecallBand publishes a [0,0] band for an arm with zero (or sub-min_n) labelled findings — it guards the OTHER arm's denominator but never its own numerator's support
samples.evidence: `relativeRecallBand` only refuses when `otherLabelled === 0` (line 613) or when `real + otherReal === 0` (623), and suppresses only on `unionLow < minN` (628). It never receives or checks THIS arm's own labelled count. So with `real = 0` and the other arm's `otherReal >= minN` it falls through to the reported branch and emits `low = 0/unionHigh`, `high = 0/unionLow`, i.e. a published band of [0.000, 0.000]. That is reachable on a real path from `scoreValidity`: line 833 registers `realByArmTier` for EVERY tier that has a label on the arm, including an arm whose labels all failed the join (all `stale-parse`, all `parse-vintage-unknown`, or `claims-not-supplied`, where `{real: 0, labelled: 0}` is stored), and line 890 then passes `real: 0` with the other arm's healthy `otherLabelled`. The report prints `BAND [0.000, 0.000]` — "this reviewer found 0% of confirmed defects" — as a property of the labelling/join, which is exactly the mirror image of the [1,1] tautology the function documents itself as refusing. The same hole publishes a band from a 1- or 2-label arm (real=1, other=20 → reported [0.048, 0.05]) even though the corresponding precision cell for that arm is suppressed at n < min_n.

samples.summary: CLI ignores --arm when reading labels: the unselected arm's labels are scored with no claim population, so --arm panel/coderabbit always reports a bogus arm, verdict PARTIAL and exit code 1
samples.evidence: Line 1096-1098 reads ALL finding labels for the corpus version (`readFindingLabels` enumerates every arm directory) and filters only by `--item`. `wantPanel`/`wantCodeRabbit` (1076-1077) gate only which CLAIM populations are built (1101-1140). `scoreValidity` then unions arms from claims and labels (line 773), so with `--arm panel` the coderabbit labels appear as an arm with `claims_supplied: false`, `claims-not-supplied` on every label (join branch at line ~419), a `reasons` entry at line 815, `completeness.verdict = "partial"` and therefore `process.exitCode = 1` (line 1160). Combined with the relative-recall hole above, it also prints a `[0.000, 0.000]` recall band for the arm the operator explicitly excluded. `--arm` is documented as a supported selector, so every single-arm invocation is misreported and non-zero-exiting.

samples.summary: claimPopulation is computed once per ARM but applied to per-TIER cells, so a gold-tier stratum can be declared permanently not-measurable and its reason can state something false
samples.evidence: `claimPopulation` (line 793) is `exhausted` when every distinct claim of the arm carries a label of ANY tier. It is then passed unchanged into every per-tier cell (lines 842-843, 863). With a mixed arm — e.g. 10 keys labelled `gold`, 20 labelled `silver`, all 30 labelled — the tier=gold / stratum=major cell has `labelled_findings: 0` and `availabilityFor` returns `not-measurable` (line 348-352), i.e. "the corpus can never answer this", even though 5 of the silver-labelled claims were judged major and a gold judgement for those keys is still obtainable. The reason string built at line 868 then asserts `every one of <arm>'s 30 distinct claim(s) ... is labelled and none was judged major`, which is simply untrue at the arm level in that case. This is the very pooling (`not-measurable` vs `not-computed`) the module's header says must never happen; the fix is to earn exhaustion per (arm, tier).

samples.summary: CLI panel branch ignores `population_state` and `dropped` from runRecords, so an absent panel payload silently empties the claim population and its labels are then misdiagnosed as "the reviewer's wording moved"
samples.evidence: Line 1122 does `for (const rd of runRecords(...)) records.push(...rd.records)` with no check on `rd.population_state`, while the CodeRabbit branch at 1133 explicitly excludes and reports anything that is not `"present"`. `adapters/panel.mjs:135` returns `{state: "absent", records: []}` whenever `payload.findings` is not an array (and `panelRecords` returns `population_state` from it), and dropped findings (`panel.mjs:139`) also silently shrink the population. Because the item's envelope status can be `ok` while its payload is unusable, those claims vanish from `claimCensus`, and every label about them then joins as `unmatched` with the reason text at line 818 ("either a different replicate set or a reviewer's wording moved") — a wrong diagnosis of a readable, recorded absence.

samples.summary: claimCensus can leave a claim out of every stated-severity bucket, which makes the `stated === 0` reason assert the arm never raised that severity
samples.evidence: Lines 382-388: buckets are pre-seeded from `KNOWN` + `stated-severity-varies` and incremented only `if (Object.hasOwn(byStated, bucket))`. A record whose `severity` is absent or off-scale is still counted in `records`/`distinct_finding_keys` but lands in no bucket, so the buckets no longer sum to the distinct-key count. Line 869 then reads `stated === 0` as proof that "the arm raised no finding it called <severity> either — so no denominator for this stratum exists on this corpus", which is a permanent-unanswerability claim derived from an under-count rather than from an absence. Off-scale severities should be given their own named bucket (as `stated-severity-varies` is) instead of being dropped.

samples.summary: A supplied-but-empty claim population yields the self-contradictory reason "0 claim(s) remain unlabelled and one may still land here"
samples.evidence: Line 793 falls to `pending` when `claims.distinct_finding_keys === 0` (an arm supplied with legs that produced no keyed records), because the `exhausted` branch additionally requires `distinct_finding_keys > 0`. `unlabelledClaims` is then 0, and the reason built at line 870 prints `; 0 claim(s) remain unlabelled and one may still land here` — a sentence that contradicts its own number. The same arm's `unlabelled_claims: 0` in `armRows` (line 807) alongside `claim_population: "pending"` is equally contradictory.

samples.summary: Relative recall picks "the other arm" with ARMS.find(a => a !== armId), which silently chooses one arbitrary arm if a third is ever added
samples.evidence: Line 888: `const otherArm = ARMS.find((a) => a !== armId);`. `ARMS` is frozen at two values today (`finding-record.mjs:50`), but this is the union denominator of a published metric: with a third arm the union would silently be built from ONE of the other two, producing a band that looks computed and is wrong, with nothing in the payload naming the omitted arm. A `pin`-style assertion that `ARMS.length === 2` (the pattern this directory already uses for load-bearing literals) would fail loudly instead.

samples.summary: `min_n_source` reports the spec default when the operator explicitly passes the same value
samples.evidence: Line 909: `min_n_source: minN === MIN_N ? "spec §4.1 default, imported from segmentation.mjs" : "operator override"`. `--min-n 5` is an operator override that reads as the imported default, so the provenance field the report prints (renderReport line ~1000) is wrong for that invocation. The CLI knows whether the flag was present (`args["min-n"] === undefined`) and could pass the provenance in.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checked particular. `relativeRecallBand` (validity.mjs:597) takes no `labelled` count for its own arm; its only guards are `otherLabelled === 0` (613), `real + otherReal === 0` (623), and `unionLow < minN` (628) where `unionLow = Math.max(real, otherReal)` (626). With `real = 0` and the other arm's `otherReal >= minN`, all three guards pass and the function returns `availability: "reported"` with `low = 0/unionHigh` and `high = 0/unionLow`, i.e. a published [0,0] band (637-646). This is reachable from `scoreValidity`: `tiers` is built from every tier with a label on the arm regardless of join outcome (798, with the comment at 794-797 stating this intent), and `realByArmTier` at 833 counts only rows that reached `JOINED` (787), so an arm whose labels are all `claims-not-supplied` (420-421), `parse-vintage-unknown` (422-423) or `stale-parse` (424-425) stores `{real: 0, labelled: 0}`; line 890 then passes `real: 0` together with the healthy other arm's `theirs.labelled`, satisfying the 613 guard via the wrong arm. The report renders it as `BAND [0.000, 0.000]` (1008) — the exact mirror of the [1,1] tautology the docstring at 590-595 says it refuses to print, and inconsistent with `precisionCell` (842), which suppresses the same arm's cell below min_n. The 1-2-label variant (real=1, otherReal=20 -> reported [0.048, 0.05]) follows from the same missing own-support check. Real broken invariant / misleading published metric in the correctness lane; no guard elsewhere prevents it.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end in the repo. validity.mjs:1096 calls readFindingLabels(root, corpusVersion) with no arm option, and adjudicate.mjs:566 enumerates every arm directory, so labels for BOTH arms are loaded. Line 1098 filters only by --item; the arm selection (wantPanel/wantCodeRabbit at 1076-1077) gates only which claim populations are built (1101-1140), and the unfiltered `labels` array is handed to scoreValidity at 1144. scoreValidity:773 unions arm ids from claims AND labels, so the excluded arm gets claims=null (784), joinLabels marks every one of its labels "claims-not-supplied" (420-421), an arm row is emitted with claims_supplied:false (802), and a completeness reason is pushed unconditionally at 814-816. Line 935 then sets verdict "partial" because reasons.length !== 0, and line 1160 sets process.exitCode = 1. --arm is a documented, validated selector (1025, 1029, 1058-1062), so every single-arm invocation over a store that has labels for both arms (the normal state, since adjudicate queues both) misreports a bogus arm and exits non-zero. No arm filter or guard exists anywhere on this path.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate. `claimPopulation` is derived exactly once per arm at validity.mjs:788-793 from a tier-agnostic `labelledKeys` set, and is then passed unchanged into every tier-scoped cell (validity.mjs:842-843, :863, :876). `availabilityFor` (validity.mjs:342-346, called from precisionCell:500) turns a zero denominator into the permanent `not-measurable` state whenever that arm-level value is `exhausted`. Mixed-tier arms are explicitly supported (tiers set built at :798, reported as `tiers_scored`/`label_sources` at :810-811; assertOneTier at :944-950 only forbids mixing within a single cell), so a gold/silver arm with all keys labelled yields gold-tier strata with labelled_findings 0 declared permanently unanswerable even though a gold judgement for the silver-labelled keys remains obtainable (one label file per (arm, key) per labels.mjs:672-686, and labels.mjs:307-310 documents the silver-prefill-to-human-gold upgrade). The reason string at :868 also asserts an arm-level fact ("every one of <arm>'s N distinct claims ... none was judged <severity>") on a tier-scoped cell, which is false when a label of another tier judged that severity. This pools `not-measurable` with `not-computed` across tiers, the exact failure the module header (:33-39) and the never-pool-tiers rule (:715-719) forbid. No guard elsewhere recomputes exhaustion per (arm, tier) — grep shows :793 is the only derivation. Real logic bug in the correctness lane, major impact (wrong published availability and a false explanatory string), no refutation ground applies.
